clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old Caucasian woman presented to the ENT clinic with a 3-month history of diffuse oral burning sensation and disabling pharyngodynia, accompanied by weight loss, asthenia, cough when lying down, hoarseness, and dyspnea. She had bilateral ocular irritation and right index finger nail inflammation. Physical examination revealed extensive mucosal ulcerations of the ventral tongue, cheeks, soft palate, uvula, and posterior oropharyngeal wall. Flexible transnasal endoscopy showed crusts on the right middle turbinate and nasopharynx with diffuse whitish pseudomembrane-covered erosions of the supraglottic area and posterior hypopharyngeal wall. Clinical examination also revealed bilateral conjunctival inflammation and three blister-type skin lesions on the arms and legs. Direct immunofluorescence analysis of a perilesional skin biopsy showed linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermo-epidermal junction, which is pathognomonic for MMP. Histopathology revealed subepithelial cleavage with rare eosinophilic infiltrate. Indirect immunofluorescence was negative. The diagnosis of MMP was confirmed on clinical and immunohistological criteria with diffuse oral, ocular, nasal, cutaneous, pharyngeal, laryngeal, and nail involvement. Treatment was initiated with intravenous dexamethasone 4 mg three times daily for 3 days, followed by oral prednisone 30 mg/day in conjunction with dapsone at escalating doses (50 mg/day week 1, 75 mg/day week 2, 100 mg/day thereafter), and letrozole 2.5 mg/day. A nasogastric feeding tube was initially necessary but was discontinued as the patient showed rapid clinical improvement in the pharynx and larynx, allowing resumption of oral intake. The patient remained in partial remission during the first 12 months with few transient cutaneous lesions but without mucosal involvement. At 18 months, she experienced a laryngeal relapse, requiring the introduction of rituximab with transitory increase of prednisone and dapsone doses, achieving good clinical response.
